record.original_question: Does a graph have a finite planar cover exactly when it embeds in the projective plane; equivalently, does K_{1,2,2,2} have no finite planar cover?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.6 A graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane; in particular, K1,2,2,2 has no finite planar cover.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite simple graphs. A graph homomorphism $p: H \to G$ is called a covering projection (and $H$ is called a cover of $G$) if $p$ is surjective and, for every vertex $v \in V(H)$, the restriction of $p$ to the neighborhood of $v$ in $H$ is a bijection onto the neighborhood of $p(v)$ in $G$. A finite planar cover of $G$ is a cover $H$ of $G$ such that $H$ is finite and embeds in the plane.

A graph $G$ is said to embed in the projective plane if it has a topological embedding into the real projective plane $\mathbb{RP}^2$. Let $K_{1,2,2,2}$ denote the complete multipartite graph on parts of sizes $1, 2, 2, 2$ (equivalently, the graph on $7$ vertices obtained from $K_7$ by removing a perfect matching on $6$ of its vertices).

Prove or disprove: a connected graph $G$ admits a finite planar cover if and only if $G$ embeds in the projective plane. Equivalently, show that $K_{1,2,2,2}$ has no finite planar cover.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Negami) remains open as of 2024–2025. It is known to reduce to showing that K_{1,2,2,2} has no finite planar cover, and recent work (e.g., arXiv:2311.01672 and arXiv:2412.19560, December 2024) establishes that K_{1,2,2,2} has no n-fold planar cover for small n (n ≤ 12, with extensions toward n < 14) and proves structural constraints on any hypothetical planar cover, but the full conjecture is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Planar cover - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The one remaining graph for which this has not yet been done is K_{1,2,2,2}. If K_{1,2,2,2} could be shown not to have any planar covers, this would complete a proof of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is reduced to showing K_{1,2,2,2} has no planar cover and remains open.

status_evidence.title: K_{1,2,2,2} has no n-fold planar cover graph for n<14
status_evidence.snippet: For n ≤ 12, no n-fold cover of the graph K_{1,2,2,2} is planar.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: nonexistence of small planar covers of K_{1,2,2,2}.

status_evidence.title: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Structural properties of such planar covers (if they exist), of arbitrary fold; minimal planar cover of K_{1,2,2,2} (if it exists) must be 4-connected.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2024 work establishes structural constraints but does not close the conjecture.
